summary: The ORIGINAL emits exactly 0,0,0 on every pixel in every frame under every configuration tried (silent null output, subtype (c)) — no comparison against the port is obtainable, so the score 0 records 'no comparison', not port quality; the port itself renders a lively, beat-locked centered spectrum with all three dials live.
observations: Original side: compileError null, runtimeError null, wantsSensors true, sensors 'synth' (beat120) — it compiles, runs, binds sensor globals, and still outputs nothing. statsSummary over the 60 s / 10 fps survey: meanBrightness {avg 0, min 0, max 0}, motion {avg 0, max 0}, zeroMotionFrames 600/600.

Confirmed as exact zeros, not sub-quantum dimness rounding to 0: a --dump at 8 beat-offset times (0.15, 0.25, 0.40, 1.15, 2.35, 5.70, 8.10, 11.55 s) over a 12 s / 20 fps run gives the original 0 non-zero pixels out of 256 at every one of the 8 times, max channel 0, channel sum 0. The port at the same 8 frames has 20-176 lit pixels with max channel 255.

Original stays black across: default rig (16x16 grid), --rig strip --pixels 60, --rig grid --grid 8x8; --sensors synth and --sensors off; --seed 1 and --seed 1234; --wall-clock 1756000000 and 1756040000; --fps 20 and --fps 40; --skip 0, 30 and 200 (i.e. 4000 rendered frames of warm-up at 20 fps, ruling out a long frame-counted transient).

Original stays black at every dial setting tried: --probe-controls reports maxDelta 0.00 / maxDeltaLit 0.00 for all three sliders (byte-identical renders at 0, 0.5 and 1); a 10-point manual sweep of sliderSilenceLevel (0, 0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8, 0.95, 1) is black at every point; and four all-three-dials-pinned combinations (SilenceLevel/Fill/PeakDropSpeed = 0/0.5/0.5, 0.5/0.5/0.5, 1/1/0.5, 0/1/0) are black too — so this is not the known 'dial only works once a second control is set' setter-interaction artefact.

Harness sanity: other slugs' baseline runs in tools/verify/out have healthy original meanBrightness (1d-aurora-borealis 19.2, 1-usflag-blink 144.3, 1-white-fade 193, 2-colors 43, 2d-bouncing-additive-primaries 21.8, 2d-canvas-example 14.9), so the dead original is specific to this pattern, not a broken orig-side pipeline.

Control SURFACES match exactly on both sides: sliderSilenceLevel, sliderFill, sliderPeakDropSpeed, all kind 'slider', same order, same labels (SilenceLevel / Fill / PeakDropSpeed). No missing, extra, renamed or retyped control.

PORT (solo description, no reference to compare against): a horizontally-mirrored 'centered spectrum'. On the 16x16 grid each row is a frequency band and a bar grows symmetrically left and right from the grid's horizontal centre; the innermost/loudest region is saturated red, and outer/peak cells are magenta-violet (meanR avg 60.7 vs meanG 2.4 / meanB 11.2 at baseline — a red-dominant palette with a purple accent, no green).

PORT temporal behaviour is correctly beat-locked to the synthetic beat120 feed: port-rhythm.png shows ~12 evenly spaced horizontal bands across the 6 s baseline window = 2.0 Hz, matching the feed's 120 BPM, with a fast attack and visible exponential decay between hits. The 60 s survey rhythm shows the same cadence uniformly end-to-end with no regime/mode structure and no drift, so there are no separate regimes to park a --skip run in.

PORT steady state is healthy, not decaying: over 60 s at 10 fps meanBrightness avg 31.9 (baseline 6 s avg 24.9), zeroMotionFrames 1/600 (the unavoidable first frame), brightnessTrend 'volatile' (which is the correct reading for a 2 Hz strobing spectrum, not instability). A --skip 200 s late window is brighter still (mean 48), so nothing dies over time.

PORT goes fully black with --sensors off (mean 0, motion 0) — it is entirely sensor-driven with no free-running fallback. Whether that matches the original is unknowable here since the original is black fed OR unfed.

dials.name: sliderSilenceLevel
dials.origEffect: unverifiable from output — original renders exactly black at every value; probe maxDelta 0.00 and a 10-point manual sweep (0 to 1) all produce identical all-zero frames
dials.portEffect: live and monotonic: raises the noise-gate floor, so more of the spectrum is suppressed as it rises. 10 s / 20 fps runs give port meanBrightness 36 at 0, 17 at 0.5, 12 at 1 (motion 19 / 17 / 12). Strongest of the three dials (probe maxDelta 23.76, maxDeltaLit 79.44).

dials.name: sliderFill
dials.origEffect: unverifiable from output — original black at 0, 0.5 and 1 (probe maxDelta 0.00)
dials.portEffect: live and monotonic: controls how solidly each band's bar is filled in from the centre. At 0 the bars read as thin segments with a gap at the centre column; at 1 they are solid blocks spanning centre-outwards. 10 s / 20 fps port meanBrightness 15 / 22 / 28 at 0 / 0.5 / 1 (motion 10 / 17 / 20). Probe maxDelta 21.41, maxDeltaLit 71.01.

dials.name: sliderPeakDropSpeed
dials.origEffect: unverifiable from output — original black at 0, 0.5 and 1 (probe maxDelta 0.00)
dials.portEffect: live: governs how fast the magenta peak markers fall back after a beat. Faster drop = less lingering lit area, so mean brightness falls as the dial rises: 10 s / 20 fps port meanBrightness 28 / 24 / 20 at 0 / 0.5 / 1. Weakest of the three (probe maxDelta 13.25, maxDeltaLit 41.53) since it only affects the peak-marker cells, not the bars.

feedback: This is an ORIGINAL-side blocker, not a port defect. Nothing about the port can be scored until the original renders something: it compiles and runs clean but writes exactly 0,0,0 to all 256 pixels on all 600 frames of a 60 s survey, in every rig / seed / clock / fps / skip / dial configuration probed. Classify as orig-unrenderable subtype (c), silent null output.

Likely engine-gap direction to investigate (not a port fix): the original is flagged wantsSensors:true and is fed the identical beat120 signal the port reacts to, so the zeroing happens downstream of the sensor bind. Suspect a sensor-derived expression that evaluates to 0 or NaN on our engine — e.g. a normalisation by maxFrequencyMagnitude/energyAverage, a log/sqrt of a value our feed leaves at 0, an unsupported array builtin over frequencyData silently yielding zeros, or an hsv/rgb call whose value term collapses. Instrumenting the original's per-band bar height on the engine would localise it in one step.

Re-run this slug's verification once the original renders. The port is a plausible, healthy implementation and deserves a real comparison: it draws a centre-mirrored per-row spectrum, locks cleanly to the 2 Hz beat, exposes exactly the original's three sliders with the same names/kinds, and each slider moves the output in an intuitive direction (SilenceLevel gates, Fill solidifies, PeakDropSpeed shortens peak decay).

Specific things to check against the original once it is renderable, since they are the port's most characterisable properties: (1) the palette — the port is red-dominant with magenta-violet peak markers and essentially zero green (meanG avg 2.4 vs meanR 60.7); (2) the mirror axis — the port mirrors LEFT/RIGHT about the grid's horizontal centre with one frequency band per row; (3) the beat response — the port's bars attack instantly and decay across the ~0.5 s beat interval; (4) the dead-sensor fallback — the port renders fully black with sensors off rather than idling on anything.
